title: A Star Is Eating Its Neighbour. The Meal Lasts Billions of Years

scenes.text: A star is eating its neighbour. The meal lasts billions of years.
Three hundred light years away, a small red star and a brown dwarf circle each other every 87 minutes.
Their whole orbit would fit inside our Sun.
Every second, the star strips off gas weighing a trillion burritos. That's MIT's comparison, not ours.
The star is so small it sips instead of gulping. Nobody had seen that before.
So the brown dwarf won't be swallowed today. Just bite by bite, for billions of years.

description:
A star is eating its neighbour, and the meal will last billions of years.
MIT astronomers found a small red star about 300 light years away pulling gas off a brown dwarf that orbits it every 87 minutes, an orbit so tight it would fit inside the Sun. It is the first time a low-mass star has been caught slowly feeding on another low-mass object, published in Nature Astronomy in October 2026.
If you could watch one event in space in fast-forward, what would it be?
first_comment: Bonus: the star weighs about 85 Jupiters and the brown dwarf about 25. Our Sun is more than a thousand Jupiters. If you could watch one event in space in fast-forward, what would it be?
